title: Flat scalar evaluation on an arbitrary first complex and its derived coherence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of commutative ring sheaves, $E=S\otimes_R-$ exact ordinary scalar extension, and $U$ termwise scalar restriction on complexes and derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use unbounded localization $Q$, $E^{\mathbf L}$, normalized derived tensor-Hom structures $H_R,H_S$, and simultaneous scalar tensor comparisons with their K-flat representative square [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data]. Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat $R$-complex, $J$ a K-injective $R$-complex, $D$ any $R$-complex, and $b:D\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$ a chain map [def-pc-kflat-complex] [def-pur-kinjective-complex] [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. Write $\widetilde b:D\otimes_R P\to J$ for chain evaluation $x\otimes p\mapsto b(x)(p)$, and $\beta:QD\to H_R(QP,QJ)$ for its derived transpose. Put $A=S\otimes_R D$. Under the canonical exact-extension representative identifications $E^{\mathbf L}QM\cong Q(EM)$ and $S\otimes_R M\cong UEM$, the map obtained from $UE^{\mathbf L}([\widetilde b])$ by the inverse scalar tensor comparison and the scalar unit on $QP$ is represented by the actual chain map $h_b:A\otimes_R P\to UEJ$, $(s\otimes x)\otimes p\mapsto s\otimes b(x)(p)$. This assertion holds for arbitrary $D$, including $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$; neither $D$ nor $A$ is required to be K-flat. For every flat-term K-flat resolution $t:V\to D$, the representative square for $V,P$ descends along the quasi-isomorphisms $Et$, $E(t\otimes1_P)$ and $t\otimes1_P$ to this same formula, independently of $t$.

For arbitrary derived inputs $K,L$, let $c^\varphi_{K,L}:E^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\to H_S(E^{\mathbf L}K,E^{\mathbf L}L)$ be the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, and let $\Theta$ be the evaluation-normalized scalar adjunction [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. The derived transpose of $\Theta U(c^\varphi_{QP,QJ})\circ UE^{\mathbf L}(\beta)$ is $[h_b]$. The comparison $c^\varphi$ is natural in both arbitrary derived inputs, including morphisms represented by inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. For $R\xrightarrow{\varphi}S\xrightarrow{\psi}T$ with exact scalar extensions, $c^{\psi\varphi}$ equals $c^\psi\circ E_\psi^{\mathbf L}(c^\varphi)$ under the canonical scalar-composition identifications on its source and both Hom inputs; the identity coefficient comparison is the identity. The representative formula above respects these identifications and both paths of compatible coefficient squares. No boundedness, finite freeness or filtered-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Write $F=E^{\mathbf L}$, and write $\mu_{X,Y}:F(X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}FX\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}FY$ for the specified normalized tensor comparison. Exactness of $E$ implies that $E$ carries every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism, by the cohomology comparison. The exact-functor factorization and its left-derived universal property, together with the statement that $F$ is the left derived functor of termwise scalar extension computed by K-flat resolutions, therefore identify $FQM$ naturally with $QEM$ for every complex $M$, not just for K-flat ones (uniqueness of left derived functors). This identification is the canonical one: on a K-flat resolution $t:V\to M$, both comparison maps commute with $Qt$ and $QEt$, and those are invertible. Restriction $U$ leaves the underlying complexes of abelian sheaves unchanged; hence it also preserves quasi-isomorphisms. In particular $Et$ and $U\!Et$ are quasi-isomorphisms whenever $t$ is.

proof.text: The one-K-flat-factor transpose lemma, with $A=D$ and target $J$, identifies $QD\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP$ with $Q(D\otimes_R P)$ and gives $\operatorname{ev}_R\circ(\beta\otimes1_{QP})=Q\widetilde b$. The same lemma with arbitrary first complex $A=S\otimes_R D$ identifies $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP$ with $Q(A\otimes_R P)$. Neither application imposes K-flatness on its first complex. The chain identification $\nu_D:S\otimes_R D\cong UED$ is fixed by $s\otimes x\mapsto s\otimes x$. The scalar-chain Hom identification supplies $\alpha_S(s\otimes f)(p)=s\otimes f(p)$. Composing it with $S\otimes b$ and evaluating gives the actual chain map $h_b((s\otimes x)\otimes p)=s\otimes b(x)(p)$. These are sheafification-unit generators in each total summand, not arbitrary choices of sections.

proof.text: For the scalar-unit map $\lambda_{X,K}:UX\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to U(X\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}FK)$, fix $X=QEV$ with $V$ K-flat and $K=QP$. Its scalar adjunct is $(\varepsilon_X\otimes1)\circ\mu_{UX,K}$; this is the five-bijection map in the scalar adjunction. Resolve $UEV$ by a flat-term K-flat complex $w:W\to UEV$. By representative-normalized scalar adjunction the adjunct of $Qw$ is represented by $\bar w:EW\to EV$, $s\otimes z\mapsto s\,w(z)$. The normalized tensor square for $W,P$ therefore says that $\lambda_{X,QP}$, precomposed by $Q(w\otimes1_P)$, is represented by $z\otimes p\mapsto w(z)\otimes(1\otimes p)$. Here both $EW,EP$ are K-flat by the given scalar comparison, as is $EV$. The one-factor tensor theorem makes $w\otimes1_P$ a quasi-isomorphism and computes its target without requiring $UEV$ to be K-flat. Cancel it. Hence $\lambda_{QEV,QP}$ itself is represented by $a_{V,P}:UEV\otimes_R P\to U(EV\otimes_S EP)$, $y\otimes p\mapsto y\otimes(1\otimes p)$. This verifies the scalar-unit representative used next.

proof.text: First replace $D$ by a flat-term K-flat complex $V$ with a quasi-isomorphism $t:V\to D$, and put $b_V=b\circ t$. On the pair $V,P$ use the assumed K-flat representative square for $\mu$. Denote its actual chain isomorphism by $m_{V,P}:E(V\otimes_R P)\cong EV\otimes_S EP$. After restriction and insertion of the scalar unit on $P$, its inverse sends $(s\otimes v)\otimes p$ to $s\otimes(v\otimes p)$: the tensor comparison sends $1\otimes(v\otimes p)$ to $(1\otimes v)\otimes(1\otimes p)$, and $S$-linearity gives the assertion for $s$. Applying $E(\widetilde b_V)$ gives $s\otimes b(t(v))(p)$. Thus the normalized derived composite on $QV,QP$ is represented by $h_{b_V}$. The representative square includes preservation of K-flatness by extension. No K-flatness claim about $\mathcal Hom(P,J)$ has entered this calculation.

proof.text:
For any such $t$, the map $t\otimes1_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the K-flat tensor invariance theorem. Consequently $Et$ and $E(t\otimes1_P)$ are quasi-isomorphisms by step 1. Also $(U\!Et)\otimes1_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism by that same tensor invariance theorem. Naturality of $\mu$, of its representative square and of the scalar unit identifies the step-4 composite precomposed with $Q((U\!Et)\otimes1_P)$ with the composite for $D$ so precomposed. On chains,
$$h_b\circ((U\!Et)\otimes1_P)=UE(\widetilde b)\circ UE(t\otimes1_P)\circ U(m_{V,P}^{-1})\circ a_{V,P};$$
both sides send $(s\otimes v)\otimes p$ to $s\otimes b(t(v))(p)$. After localization cancel the invertible precomposition. The result is precisely $Qh_b$ on $Q(A\otimes_R P)$. This proves descent along the three asserted quasi-isomorphisms and independence of $t$: every resolution gives the same explicitly defined chain map. Existence of at least one such resolution was step 4.

proof.text:
For any derived object $X$ put $\lambda_{X,K}:UX\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to U(X\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}FK)$ for the restriction/scalar-unit map occurring in the evaluation normalization of $\Theta$. That normalization and naturality of this map in $X$ give
$$\operatorname{ev}_R\circ((\Theta\,U(c^\varphi_{K,L})\,UF\beta)\otimes1_K)
=U(\operatorname{ev}_S\circ(c^\varphi_{K,L}\otimes1_{FK}))\circ\lambda_{FH_R(K,L),K}\circ(UF\beta\otimes1_K)
=UF(\operatorname{ev}_R)\circ U(\mu^{-1}_{H_R(K,L),K})\circ\lambda_{FH_R(K,L),K}\circ(UF\beta\otimes1_K)
=UF(\operatorname{ev}_R\circ(\beta\otimes1_K))\circ U(\mu^{-1}_{QD,K})\circ\lambda_{FQD,K}.$$
The middle equality is the defining transpose equation for $c^\varphi$; the last is naturality of $\mu$ and $\lambda$. Here $\beta:QD\to H_R(K,L)$. For $K=QP,L=QJ$, step 2 identifies the last evaluation with $Q\widetilde b$, and steps 3-5 identify this composite with $Qh_b$. This proves the asserted derived transpose equation by the specified normalization of $\Theta$.

proof.text:
Naturality can be checked wholly inside the derived categories. Let $f:K'\to K$ and $g:L\to L'$ be arbitrary derived morphisms. The desired equation is
$$H_S(Ff,Fg)\circ c^\varphi_{K,L}=c^\varphi_{K',L'}\circ F(H_R(f,g)).$$
Transpose both sides with respect to the right tensor factor $FK'$. The first transpose is
$$Fg\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{R;K,L})\circ\mu^{-1}_{H_R(K,L),K}\circ(1\otimes Ff).$$
Naturality of $\mu$ changes this to $F(g\circ\operatorname{ev}_{R;K,L}\circ(1\otimes f))\circ\mu^{-1}_{H_R(K,L),K'}$. The evaluation identity $g\circ\operatorname{ev}_{R;K,L}\circ(1\otimes f)=\operatorname{ev}_{R;K',L'}\circ(H_R(f,g)\otimes1)$ and naturality of $\mu$ give the transpose of the second side. Injectivity of the closed Hom-bijection proves the equation. These are exactly the naturality and evaluation equations in the specified closed structures, so no assertion about representing all derived maps by single chain maps is needed.

proof.text: In particular step 7 applies to $f=(Qq)^{-1}$ or $g=(Qq)^{-1}$ for any quasi-isomorphism $q$. Equivalently, take the naturality equation for $Qq$ and multiply on the appropriate side by its inverse; functoriality gives $F((Qq)^{-1})=F(Qq)^{-1}$ and the same identity for the Hom actions. Since localization makes each $Qq$ invertible, this is a valid equation for the actual derived morphisms. Composing the equations proves naturality for their composites as well. Thus the representative calculation is compatible with changing representatives and with inverse quasi-isomorphisms, not just with chain maps.

proof.text:
For $R\xrightarrow{\varphi}S\xrightarrow{\psi}T$, write $F=E_\varphi^{\mathbf L}$ and $G=E_\psi^{\mathbf L}$ and identify $E_{\psi\varphi}^{\mathbf L}$ with $GF$ by the canonical unit-normalized scalar-composition isomorphism. The tensor coherence theorem identifies $\mu^{\psi\varphi}$ with $\mu^\psi\circ G\mu^\varphi$ with these same transports. Transpose $c^\psi_{FK,FL}\circ G(c^\varphi_{K,L})$. Its evaluation, on $GFH_R(K,L)\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}GFK$, is
$$G(\operatorname{ev}_S)\circ(\mu^\psi)^{-1}\circ(Gc^\varphi\otimes1)
=G(\operatorname{ev}_S\circ(c^\varphi\otimes1))\circ(\mu^\psi)^{-1}
=GF(\operatorname{ev}_R)\circ G((\mu^\varphi)^{-1})\circ(\mu^\psi)^{-1}.$$
The first equality is naturality of $\mu^\psi$ and the second is the transpose equation for $c^\varphi$. Tensor coherence makes the last expression $E_{\psi\varphi}^{\mathbf L}(\operatorname{ev}_R)\circ(\mu^{\psi\varphi})^{-1}$, including its source and two Hom-input transports. This is the defining transpose of $c^{\psi\varphi}$, so injectivity of transposition proves the coefficient composition equation. Exactness is only needed for the earlier chain representatives.

proof.text: The identity part of tensor coherence identifies $\mu^{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity tensor comparison under scalar multiplication. Thus the defining transpose of $c^{\mathrm{id}}$ is evaluation itself, which is the transpose of the identity on internal Hom. Hence $c^{\mathrm{id}}=1$. The scalar adjunction isomorphisms have the same evaluation normalization and commute with coefficient changes, so applying $\Theta$ to the equations of steps 7 and 9 retains those equations. For a compatible coefficient square, apply step 9 along each of its two paths: their composite ring maps agree, so both yield the comparison for that common map under the canonical composition identifications.

proof.text: At the level of actual representatives the composition identification is $t\otimes(s\otimes x)\mapsto t\psi(s)\otimes x$, with inverse inserting $1$. Applying the formula for $h_b$ twice gives $t\otimes(s\otimes b(x)(p))$, hence $t\psi(s)\otimes b(x)(p)$ after this identification. This is the single-extension formula, and the identity case is $r\otimes b(x)(p)\mapsto r b(x)(p)$. More generally in a square $R\xrightarrow{\varphi}S$, $R'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}S'$ with $a:R\to R'$, $d:S\to S'$ and $d\varphi=\varphi'a$, the coefficient coherence for the actual chain Hom maps supplies the extension and restriction transports. Its formula $r'\otimes(s\otimes z)\mapsto\varphi'(r')d(s)\otimes(1\otimes z)$ sends the evaluated section to $\varphi'(r')d(s)\otimes(1\otimes b(x)(p))$ on both paths. Thus the generator formula respects those specified maps, including their Hom-input transports. Localizing and using steps 5 and 9-10 gives the corresponding derived identifications whenever the exact-extension representatives of the statement are used. All arguments allow unbounded complexes, $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$, and zero coefficients.
